scope: Unity workspace policy and retention planning; issue #859 remains unfinished.
evidence: Original 63-control native driver passes before migration and from its byte-verified frozen source against the migrated adapter.
Each host executes both the original frozen implementation and current adapter for 61 captured cases and three additional boundary cases; Windows results remain pending at capture.
The 48 existing framework workspace controls pass without native Unity, MCP calls or runner filesystem changes.
A regression reproduced eager conversion of an unused malformed size; the typed planner now converts only consumed sizes.
Three red native boundary cases prove ignored Unicode mode comparison, leading child separators and lexical dot preservation before their fixes.
The first frozen-driver seal check rejected normalized line endings; restoring original CRLF bytes matches the recorded original hash.
Protocol errors, BOM provenance encodings, linked ancestors, bounded provenance reads and nonfinite prune observations are covered.
Three review controls reproduced an unreadable-pointer false absence and two nonfinite native early-return bypasses. Explicit stat errors and native finite checks correct these failures.
The native path adapter normalizes both separator forms; Windows execution of the frozen comparisons remains a CI gate, not an inferred success.

Five native exit-status controls fail before correction and pass afterward: successful and failed calls preserve prior or undefined global LASTEXITCODE, and actual child status is read despite a caller-local shadow. The adapter captures the prior scalar before invocation and restores it in finally.
A planning exception reproduced a fatal best-effort prune before correction. Planning failure now logs and returns before deletion; workspace-resolution and retention errors remain fatal.
native_exceptions: PowerShell host comparison, DateTime conversion and Sort-Object ordering marshal ordered candidates without replacing culture or unstable equal-key behavior.
Native Directory.Move owns the retention mutation and preserves its no-replacement failure behavior. It adds path diagnostics without retrying failures.
The existing Invoke-PersistentProjectPrune retains DriveInfo space measurement, native directory metadata and Remove-Item deletion semantics; its budget plan delegates to typed Python.
retained_limits: This family does not prove the complete #859 scripting inventory migrated.
Planning and directory movement are separate phases; no atomic check-and-move guarantee or rollback is introduced.
The known self-hosted Windows runner lock remains external; diagnostics improve the next failure but do not identify or release its holder.
Owned symlink tests skip only when Windows denies fixture creation; existing junction controls remain in the frozen native driver.
An independent native writer must remain idle during retention; no deletion, handle killing or fresh-project fallback is introduced.

measurement.filesystem: Owned worktree: tmpfs; measured deep shared artifact fixture: Windows-backed 9p mount. No native Unity execution.
measurement.method: One existing PowerShell parent, two warmup pairs then seven alternating original/typed pairs. Dot-source outside each timed operation; actual decisions and no-retention result checked.
notes: All startup regressions retained. The deep shared artifact path is the measured retention fixture; no shallow-path or Windows extrapolation.
Inherited VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch diagnostic is included in the timed uv calls; uv selects the explicit owned project environment.
Earlier paired captures are retained with their original rows; current capture follows the native exit-status correction.
No statistical significance, full-job improvement or runner-lock recovery is claimed.

source_scope: Current integration-validation inputs only. Historical maps and timing captures remain immutable and do not attest current-head performance.
